Dear ISMAEL*,* 

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *3 September 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Documents*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

Hi [~accountid:6332c7ab409249995ee9c5e8] Thank you for granting me access to the document. 

Quick question, in the summary you mention *_“This programme will include driver training to educate drivers on how to assist riders with disabilities and to mitigate our liability”_*

What do you mean by “mitigate our liability” can you expand on this please? 

* is this reduce the amount of customer service complaints we receive? 
* reduce the court claims Bolt receives? 

In addition, if say a driver does not assist a passenger (when the passenger has booked Bolt Assist) and the passenger complains to Bolt how will that complaint be resolved? I am just trying to think of all possible scenarios so would be helpful to understand how these situations will be handled. I know in the past we have received complaints from passengers who felt that a driver may have “discriminated” against them because of their disability, so it would be good to know the extent Bolt will be liable for this as the current stance we take is that passengers should make a claim against drivers and drivers should make a claim against the passenger (as opposed to Bolt being held liable). 

Happy to discuss further if needed on Slack - thank you.

*Rebalancing - Average rides in # hours before rebalancing, compared to average rides in # hours after. Demonstrate impact and effectiveness of fleet rebalancing (24hours)* 



* Rides before rebalancing: 0.69
* Rides after rebalancing: 2.25

sql

{code:sql}
with rebalances as (
select vehicle_id , city_id,resolved_at, cast(id as varchar)||'-'||connection_id as id, resolver_id
from ng_rental.rental_order_vehicle_task
where task_type ='rebalance'
and resolver_type ='charger'
and resolved_at >date'2024-04-01' and resolved_at<date'2024-10-01'
),
 rebalances_and_gmv_before as (
select
  r.vehicle_id,
  r.city_id,
  r.resolved_at,
  r.id,
  r.resolver_id,
  date(resolved_at) as period,
  count(distinct o1.id) rides_before_rebalancing
from rebalances r
left join ng_rental.rental_order_order o1
  on o1.vehicle_id = r.vehicle_id
  and o1.created_date between date_add('hour',-96,r.resolved_at) and date_add('hour',96,r.resolved_at)
  and o1.created between date_add('minute',-1*60*24,r.resolved_at) and r.resolved_at
  and o1.state='finished'
  and o1.created_date >date'2024-04-01'  
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6
),
rebalances_and_gmv_after as (
select
  r.vehicle_id,
  r.city_id,
  r.resolved_at,
  r.id,
  date(resolved_at) as period,
  count(distinct o2.id) rides_after_rebalancing
from rebalances r
left join ng_rental.rental_order_order o2
on o2.vehicle_id = r.vehicle_id
and o2.created_date between date_add('hour',-96,r.resolved_at) and date_add('hour',96,r.resolved_at)
and o2.created between  r.resolved_at  and date_add('minute',60*24,r.resolved_at)
and o2.state='finished'
and o2.created_date >date'2024-01-01'  
group by 1,2,3,4,5
)
select city_name, avg(rides_before_rebalancing), avg(rides_after_rebalancing) from (
select
  t1.vehicle_id,
  t1.city_id,
  t1.resolved_at,
  t1.id,
  t1.resolver_id,
  t1.period,
  c.name as city_name,
  coalesce(t1.rides_before_rebalancing,0) rides_before_rebalancing,
  coalesce(t2.rides_after_rebalancing,0) rides_after_rebalancing
from rebalances_and_gmv_before t1
left join rebalances_and_gmv_after t2 on t1.vehicle_id=t2.vehicle_id and t1.resolved_at=t2.resolved_at and t1.id = t2.id and t1.period = t2.period
left join ng_public.admin_system_city c on t1.city_id=c.id
)
group by 1
{code}

*Main outputs from my review:*

⭐ If the Commerce and Product teams find a way to compensate users additionally on top of the full refund for scheduled rides, *compensation guidelines are going to be changed the most*.

* Our logic is that the Bolt Lux users should be provided with a top-class seamless luxury service, and some of the issues in our processes (for example, driver arriving to the pick-up location late, or bad vehicle condition) are *unacceptable for Bolt Lux*. That's why we have to be as generous as we can to compensate for the wasted time of the customer or if the provided service was even slightly different from what the customer expected (if you are worried about us compensating *too much* - the initial test is going to be only in 2 cities and the predicted volume of rides is very low ([@krzysztof.wielgolaski|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U0194NLSVBN]can share the numbers), so we have more space to be generous at the moment).
* This means that for some processes agents will have to offer *full refunds + additional compensation* as an apology for bad experience. Also it's possible that the cases for which a usual rider is not compensated, Bolt Lux customers are going to be compensated for.

⭐ *Traveling with a pet/child/wheelchair* - Bolt Lux cars won't be required to have additional equipment such as child seats or per carriers, but we will establish in our processes that the customer needs to contact the chauffeur before the trip to inform them that they will be traveling with a pet/child/wheelchair. The chauffeur has a right to reject the trip if they can't complete the trip if they don't have the needed equipment.

⭐ *Requesting additional destinations during the active ride* - the pricing for Bolt Lux won't be upfront - it will be based on minutes/kms that were made during the trip. This means that we can let the customer ask the chauffeur to make additional stops during the trip, even though these stops weren't added while ordering the trip - this is still not 100% confirmed though!

❓ *Pending questions at the moment:*

* Will CS be able to offer additional compensation to Bolt Lux customers? - still being investigated by [@ashok.fernandez|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U07BGNUASJG] :loading: if the Product team is not able to provide CS with such functionality, we will stick to full and partial refunds.
* Will the Bolt Lux customer be able to request additional destinations during the active ride? - still being investigated by [@ashok.fernandez|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U07BGNUASJG] :loading: 

Some questions from me:

* How drivers are going to be affected by the Bolt Lux category? Will there be special rules for Bolt Lux drivers that are different from the usual drivers (in terms of commission, blocks, payouts)? If yes, I believe I need to review existing driver processes as well - answer from Krzysztof - *_As I was informed, Lux drivers will operate exactly the same as any other driver. Block guidelines is something I am clarifying with Oliver, but otherwise all usual driver processes should apply (as far as I am aware)._* :loading: 
* Should there be a separate process for reporting chauffeur behavior issues/misconducts? At the moment the existing processes ask us to either escalate to Local OPS (where BQS is not live) or do nothing - answer from Krzysztof - *_Also as mentioned - clarifying with Oliver._* :loading: 
* Will automated compensations be enabled for Bolt Lux tickets? If yes, what kind of logic is going to be implemented there? - answer from Krzysztof - *_No automations will not be enabled for Lux tickets._* (/)

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *21 October 2024.*

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

*Rudderstack - internal summary:*

# Bolt was renewing the service agreement (SA) with an important service provider - Rudderstack - a customer data platform that enables Bolt to collect, process, and route customer data to various tools and systems.
# Rudderstack provides a default DPA where it understakes to process personal data of Bolt as a data processor (DPA under Art. 28 GDPR). *The DPA was previously reviewed and accepted by Bolt`s privacy team back in 2022.*
# Upon renewal and review of the DPA, it was spotted that the DPA is overall compliant with the GDPR / UK GDPR.
# However, it was not fully aligned with Bolt`s internal standards + it includes outdated UK SCCs, which were updated with the UK IDTA in 2022. Summary of privacy`s review is added [below|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-39713?focusedCommentId=2647855].

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Bolt requested to update the DPA to match Bolt standards & updated UK IDTA to be added. After a few rounds of negotiations, Rudderstack agreed to:*

* update reference to the outdated UK SCCs with the UK IDTA - taken from Bolt`s standard DPA template; general authorisation of international data transfers as the provider is trusted and audited;
* incorporate a few changes that bring the Rudderstack DPA closer to Bolt`s compliance. Specific updates include:
** extended notification for subprocessors to 20 days, instead of 14 days, per Bolt`s max fallback position for processors; general authorisation as the provider is trusted and audited;
** 72 hour response to DSRs from Bolts DSs instead of unspecified timeline; procedure enhanced to specify that DSs will be directed to [https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/data-subject/|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/data-subject/|smart-link] to submit DSRs to Bolt;
** return or deletion of personal data upon termination - _“as soon as reasonably practicable”_; Rudderstack will not hold Bolt's data for 180 days post termination unless requested by Bolt; this is max fallback position by Rudderstack.
** enhanced audit rights for Bolt; Bolt can request audits (including onsite audits) once per 12 months; *or* if Bolt received a notice from RudderStack of a Security Incident; *or* such an audit is required by Applicable Data Protection Laws or by Customer’s competent supervisory authority. Previously, audits were generally limited to once per 12 months.
** audit costs split in case of a negative finding of the audit revealing material deficiencies of RudderStack’s compliance obligations; previous position - Bolt covers audit costs in full.
** assistance with with DPIAs and regulatory inquiries - “reasonable assistance” at Rudderstack expense; if such reasonable cooperation will require RudderStack to assign significant resources to that effort - at Bolt`s expense.

Additionally, default TOMs by Rudderstack were reviwed and confirmed with Bolt's Infosec.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Main points of concern that were not updated due to Rudderstack fallback positions:* 

* limitation of liability not updated; currently liability is same as in the SA - limited to 12 moths fees paid by Bolt (350 000 EUR); LoL reviewed by legal and accepted by business, legal and privacy teams previously.
* data breach notification - no specific timeframe included; notification is done “without indue delay”.

The privacy team was unable to continue the negotiation, as the SA and DPA needed to be signed by the end of October to secure favorable commercial terms with Rudderstack, per the request of the business.

Given the importance of this supplier, the compliance of the terms with the GDPR framework, its strong reputation with Bolt, and its robust security measures, the privacy team chose not to create a bottleneck in the process, and conclude the negotiations.
{panel}

Thank you [@soteris.tsigarides|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UAP6YTME0].In that case, our obligations under GDPR are triggered.*What that means:*

* Under the GDPR, in these kinds of situations, we are allowed to disclose the data when we have a legal obligation to do so. I have analyzed their document, and it lacks a reference to a specific law.
* Per our internal process, best practice, and the law, the authority requesting us for data disclosure shall cite a specific provision of a specific law that obligates us to disclose personal data to them.
* To my understanding, they are requesting data of all drivers in Cyprus.
** All of driver data requested falls under the definition of personal data, thus protected by the GDPR.
* If we were to disclose such a big amount of data, we need to at least document that we have been informed by the Authority that there is a legal ground (a specific law) that obligates us to disclose this data
* If we were to disclose everything as-is without pushing back, we would be facing a major GDPR risk. If escalated, it could lead us to a regulatory investigation and bad PR would follow.

*What do I suggest doing:*

* Let's send a clear explanation to the Aurhority in a friendly tone - they have been sending us a reference to a law before, so they must know that they need to provide us with it.
* Once we receive that, we can proceed with disclosing data.

 I do understand the seriousness of this request. However, due to regulatory scrutiny we've been facing in the EU, I recommend taking these steps.

Dear Daniel,

We write in relation to the deletion of your old Bolt account on 5 October, as well as in relation to your data subject rights request that we received on 7 October 2024.

We sincerely apologise for the deletion of your old Bolt account, which was due to a human error in the implementation of our fraud detection and prevention processes. After a thorough investigation, it has been determined that, unfortunately, your previous account cannot be restored due to technical limitations. Hi [~accountid:5d91ad8a1d47a50c34d48412] according to Croatian Labour act a minor is defined as someone between 15 and 18 years old. 

The law prohibits the employment of minors *who are still in mandatory primary education*, except for tasks related to work-based learning or occasional student work, as long as these do not harm their well-being. Minors can participate in activities like film shooting, advertising, or sports competitions for payment with approval from social welfare authorities, ensuring it doesn't interfere with their health, safety, education, or development. The legal guardian must request approval 15 days in advance, and the authorities must respond within 10 days.

If a legal guardian authorizes a minor aged 15 or older (*but not attending mandatory primary education)* to enter into a specific employment contract, the minor is legally capable of entering into and terminating that contract, as well as carrying out all legal actions related to fulfilling the rights and obligations from the contract.

An employer may not hire a minor if the minor does not have authorization from their legal guardian or approval from the authority responsible for social welfare.

Therefore, fleets would need to employ minors and seek parental permission. This would need to be verified by Bolt before onboarding the courier. 

Minors cannot act as an independent contractors as they are not authorized to sign agreements.

I have discussed this also with an external counsel in Finland, who has provided the following input: 

* Finnish law does *not* specify any particular requirements regarding the form of a written notice in a contractual relationship. 
* Therefore, the parties are free to agree on the requirements in the agreement. Generally, emails (including automated emails) are considered sufficient if the other conditions for the notice agreed in the contract are met. This contract does however not contain any specific requirements beyond the written form, such as stating that emails must be sent to a certain person or that only registered mail is allowed.
* *A notice is deemed to have been received if it has reached the addressee in such a way that they have had an opportunity under normal circumstances to review it*. Therefore, if the automated messages are clear, contain the necessary information, and meet other contractual formal requirements, they can be *deemed sufficient written notices*.
* The fact that the party imposing the contractual penalties is a city does not make a difference on the assessment of requirements for “written notice” as the penalties are based on the contractual relationship between the parties. 

Based on the above, we unfortunately do not have a case to argue that we haven’t been informed duly of the infringements made and we must pay the penalties.

How to test – you can do it with whichever service or reuse the local setup with {{adummy-db}} which I’ve used:

# Checkout {{test/PIF-2101-db-pool-testing}} branch
# Compile and run {{adummy-db}}
# Get an internal auth token by following this guide: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3922756237/05.01+How+to+send+a+request+to+the+local+service|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3922756237/05.01+How+to+send+a+request+to+the+local+service|smart-link] 
# Run the first type of query: {{curl 'http://localhost/adummy-db/internal/loadItem?id=1' -H "Authorization: Basic $USER_CREDENTIALS"}}
It will try to run 30 queries simultaneously, which will fill up the DB pool.
# Check the number of connections in the pool like this: {{curl -sS 'http://localhost/adummy-db/metrics' -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' --compressed | grep 'nodejs:db:connections{'}}
It should be 20.
# Wait for a minute or so – after 1min ({{free_connection_after_ms}} * 2 = 60s) the number of connections will drop by 1 every second, up until 10 connections. This is the old behavior kicking in.
# After 12 minutes (maximum default age of the connection) connections should start disappearing from the pool *according to the new logic*. They should eventually all be removed (count should drop to 0).
## Prior to the implementation of the new logic, the connections will always stay at 10, unless you start making new requests. If you make a request to {{curl ‘http://localhost/adummy-db/internal/loadItem?id=2' -H "Authorization: Basic $USER_CREDENTIALS"}} (same as above, but {{id=2}}), which does 1 query only, the connection should be taken from the pool and recycled as “old” as soon as the request is finished, so the number of connections will be 9 now. If you keep sending requests, the number of connections will eventually go down to 0, and after the next request it will become 1. If you do nothing at any point, the connection count shouldn’t ever change.

In production, you should observe the same behavior for a service which uses DB and is rarely ever called. Go to Admin Panel, make a couple of requests to populate the DB pool, and then monitor the number of connections via Grafana: [https://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/000000001/database-connections-queries?orgId=1&refresh=1m&var-team=All&var-type=All&var-host=All&var-shard=All&var-service=chaos-testing&var-service=chaos-testing-notification&var-service=chaos-testing-automation&var-user=All&var-database=All&var-interval=$__auto_interval_interval&from=now-12h&to=now|https://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/000000001/database-connections-queries?orgId=1&refresh=1m&var-team=All&var-type=All&var-host=All&var-shard=All&var-service=chaos-testing&var-service=chaos-testing-notification&var-service=chaos-testing-automation&var-user=All&var-database=All&var-interval=$__auto_interval_interval&from=now-12h&to=now]

Hello [~accountid:614c37592a6f5a00712e7b7c], and thank you for the insight. 

First off, I fully agree that having multiple closing templates would risk making things more confusing. However, the reason why I still asked about this possibility is because the information added in the ‘new’ closing note (_the Date of Report and Event Category_), are already present in the opening note, which to me makes it redundant when both note types are used in a normal case and just adds to the clutter in Admin-Panel / Legacy when reading past reports (_this due to either Admin version not having any paragraphs in the comments and all the information just being in a single sentence_).

In short I think that adding this information when unneeded would make it harder to count precedents, not easier. For the Low / Moderate cases that are not investigated however, then I fully understand the addition of these fields and indeed it makes things easier for them since we’re omitting the entire opening comments so its a net positive.

----

You’re absolutely correct that the Global EA Tool offers just the one format, specifically the one to be used in the Admin Order if we go by the information in the KB Articles though, to be fair, the closing notes between Beehive and Admin Order have always been identical and a difference exists only in the opening notes. Even then the difference is only the addition of:

_CS Safety [Enter Your Name]:_ 
 _[Enter Reporting Party] reports_

in the beginning of the Beehive opening note, while the rest is identical between both opening note types. But it's a good thing that you mentioned the Tool, because it could be used to entirely automate the use of comments. Something like:

* If the Event is Low / Moderate *AND* the assessment *IS* being solved directly, the Tool would provide only the ‘new’ closing comment and omit the opening one;
* If the event is High / Significant, or a Low / Moderate which *ISN’T* solved without investigating then it would create the opening note, and in turn when the assessment is completed it would generate the ‘old’ closing comment to minimize duplicate information;

This would however be dependent on if its possible to setup a variable in the Tool that tracks if it has been reopened or not, which I admit I have no knowledge if its possible or not. 



All in all, it’s an optimization that I believe should be considered if possible. But as you stated, if it cannot be added in a natural / seamless way and risks creating more confusion then I entirely understand it not being considered.

*Internal comment and reasoning:* We are intentionally maintaining ambiguity because we are still in the process of assessing our use of automated decision-making (ADM). If we prematurely classify certain scenarios as involving ADM and later find they don’t meet the legal threshold of an ADM, or discover additional ADMs, it could lead to privacy or classification issues. On the other hand, saying we don’t use ADMs but later finding out that we do could also cause problems. Therefore, we're keeping our position flexible until our full assessment is complete, ensuring we can confidently address the issue across all EU countries while avoiding unnecessary double-work.

*General statement:* Like many other businesses, we are currently analysing the PWD and the practical impact on our business. As part of our analysis, our Legal and Privacy Team is assessing the overlap between the obligations under privacy legislation versus PWD and to what extent we can leverage existing processes/tools built for privacy requirements to address PWD requirements. Where possible, we will leverage what we have already built and build on this to deliver a seamless experience for our users. Unfortunately, we are not in a position to comment on specific algorithms in the light of PWD, as it is currently work in progress.

I have a doubt regarding this case, Is it not possible to disclose only the data regarding the rider, and the pick-up and drop-off exact names in the requested dates without adding any data about the driver or third parties?

Additional questions from my side:

* Am I correct to understand that we’ll be blocking chats between scammer and Driver, and only send messages to the scammer if he/she reaches out to us proactively?
* How is the manual blocking expected to work? Are there predefined scenarios where a CS agent can manually block a user, or will this be at their discretion?
* There was a mention of possibility of false positives. How will we ensure that the mark of a “scammer” is not applied to an innocent person? Also, will we be ensuring in any way that the manual blocks won’t be applied in cases of false positives?
* Will there be a process for reviewing manual blocks after they are implemented?



In general, what I see this message could contain (it might change based on responses to questions [~accountid:712020:0b1ccfcb-3809-460a-88ab-c96985ba329a] and I asked):

* We could provide a high-level reason for the anomaly without disclosing too much information. For example: "We detected unusual activity related to this order."
* We should avoid explicitly stating that the other party is a scammer or that a phishing attempt has been confirmed.
* We could offer further help or CS assistance if the victim has any questions or concerns.
* We shouldn’t add any personal data of the scammer, or add too many details on the methodology of detecting phishing. 



For manual blocks, I think it isn’t a disproportionate measure and I don’t see many issues with that, as far as our T&C clearly indicate that such actions are a violation of T&C. Also, we should have a clear process on what CS agent should be reviewing before applying manual blocks, to avoid unnecessarily punishing innocent people (i.e. false positives), and to ensure that the blocking is fair and proportionate.

Hey [~accountid:5cfe57d9a7095c0c3ffac38d], I’d like to get your opinion on this 🙏 

*Guidelines for drivers on how to correctly make a ride back to the pickup location (and get the full price)*

* My idea was to learn in which markets the price recalculation is on/off and add info to the article for each market, e.g:
** EE, LT, … : The price will get recalculated automatically, no action is needed from the driver.
** PL, NL, … : The driver needs to change the destination in-app for the price to recalculate.
** UK, UA, … : Driver needs to submit a Price Review.
* However, I see that it is difficult to understand the pricing configuration in each market, because it also varies *by city* (not only by country), and there’s no 1 definitive answer (is price recalc. on/off), there are also lots of other settings that influence the price recalculation. Also, OPS can change these settings anytime and we won’t be able to always have up-to-date info for each market. One more thing is that Bolt Send is being launched in more countries/cities, so we would also have to make sure that every new market is added to the list in the article.
* So my other idea is to simplify this and *consider that agents should be aware* of the pricing situation in their market (because they work with rides daily, do price reviews, solve cases related to price miscalculation, overcharges, etc - it would be strange if they don’t know how pricing works in their market. Also, I think this should be on their local OPS/TL to always make sure agents have the latest info about pricing in the market?)
* The simplified guidelines could look like this:
** *Price recalculation is enabled*: The price will get recalculated automatically, no action is needed from the driver.
** *Price recalculation is disabled*: The driver needs to change the destination in-app for the price to recalculate.
** *Driver is unhappy with the final price*:
*** Markets *with* Price Reviews: Ask the driver to submit PR and recalculate the price.
*** Markets *without* Price Reviews: Recalculate the price and add a manual compensation (if needed).

_This text should be included in the field below, next to the 0% tax rate – e.g. “BG VAT exempt, according to the VAT reverse charge mechanism acc. to article 44 of the EU VAT Directive / art. 21, para 2 of the Bulgarian VATA”._

Hi team, 

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount.

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

Dear Chulumanco,

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *26 September 2024*.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person.

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

In your request, you specifically asked for the call logs of the ride, which had taken place on the 8th of September 2024. Therefore, we are providing the following information regarding the personal data we hold about you, to which you are entitled:

* *A file containing call logs from a ride that had taken place on the 8th of September 2024.*

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our [https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/privacy-for-riders/|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/privacy-for-riders/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*The Data Subject’s rights*

The Data Subject has the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning him or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email. 

 

Yours sincerely,

Bolt

Hi team, 

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. For Azerbaijan, everything in Azerbaijan is centre around the e-invoice.  Say we issue 1000 promo code/coupon and we need to get €10k from the partner, then we need to issue an e-invoice to the partner to collect this €10k plus VAT.

*Problem Identified:*

* We’ve observed an average of 187K [logs|https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/r/s/XdhIE] per day where a driver is skipped due to missing precise ETAs.
* Upon investigation, it was noted that drivers were not receiving orders during specific periods.
* These errors only occur within the two-hour window before a scheduled ride.

----

*Deeper Investigation Findings:*

# *Log Context:*
#* The majority (~179K [logs|https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/r/s/A872a]) occur during the "find ride options" stage, which doesn’t directly affect real matches. This stage evaluates available options but doesn’t assign orders.
# *Impact on Matching:*
#* Only 4,850 [logs|https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/r/s/QkWcO] happen during the actual matching stage.
#* Multiple logs can be generated for a single order or driver, with a total of 440 drivers affected.

----

*What These Logs Indicate:*

* During the matching process, we calculate routes for the ~15-20 closest drivers.
* The logs represent cases where a driver with an upcoming scheduled ride was further away from the order's location compared to others (e.g., with a pickup ETA of more than 20 minutes).
* In most cases, we offer the order to the closest driver, so the logs highlight instances where more distant drivers are skipped.

----

*Conclusion and Recommendation:*

* These skipped driver logs are mostly expected behavior when prioritizing closer drivers for on-demand orders.
* There is no significant impact on matching efficiency, and drivers who experienced this issue were likely farther from the pickup location.
* Given this, I don’t see a strong case for further investigation or improvements related to this issue at this time. Drivers will still be eligible for on-demand orders if they are closer.

InnoDB’s handling of range queries and {{COUNT(*)}} operations can sometimes be less optimized than we might expect, especially for large datasets. Here’s a closer look at why InnoDB doesn’t always use key boundary differences to optimize range queries in {{COUNT(*)}}:

h3. 1. B-Tree Structure in InnoDB

InnoDB uses B+Tree indexes, where:

* Leaf nodes contain pointers to the actual rows (or entire rows if it's a clustered index).
* Range queries on B-Trees could theoretically find boundary keys, then calculate the count of nodes in the range directly by traversing the tree twice: once to locate the start of the range and once for the end.

However, MySQL’s InnoDB implementation doesn’t optimize range queries this way in most cases.

h3. 2. Row-Level Visibility and MVCC

InnoDB’s *Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC)* is one reason it avoids simple range boundary calculations. With MVCC:

* Each row may have multiple versions (snapshots) to handle transactions and isolation levels.
* For {{COUNT(*)}} within a specific range, InnoDB needs to check each row’s visibility to determine if it’s visible in the current transaction or should be ignored.
* Thus, InnoDB cannot simply rely on boundary calculations because it must iterate through the rows to apply visibility rules, ensuring an accurate count under MVCC.

h3. Summary

InnoDB’s need to ensure accuracy under MVCC rules, combined with its lack of precomputed aggregate metadata for ranges, means that it often reads each row within a range rather than using B-Tree boundaries. This ensures correctness but sacrifices potential performance optimizations for counting operations.

# *Cost Estimates*: The MySQL query optimizer uses statistical data to estimate the cost of using the index versus performing a full scan. If it estimates that the cost of multiple index lookups followed by row fetching is higher than a full scan, it will opt for the latter.

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error.

Hey, [~accountid:60f2a71843c956007065f2ad]! Thank you for reaching out. To give you a brief overview regarding this topic I would refer to Consumer Rights Directive (available [here|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2011/83/oj]). It prescribes that each member state shall outline their own language requirements, however, the main requirement of the Directive is that all information should be provided to the consumer in a clear and unambiguous manner. The Directive does not have any specific provisions referring to the customer support, but this main obligation to provide information in a clear and understandable manner could be extended to customer support. It would be a common sense that in case a local consumer is not able to speak English and we would provide information in English, then they would not be able to understand the information we are providing and hence we would be in breach of our obligation.

Considering the above when deciding whether or not to provide customer support in English by default we need to think about:

# Regulatory requirements - in this case based on analysis of Consumer Rights Directive only we have a soft push to providing customer support in local language. However, requirements coming from Romanian law are not examined and this will require us to consult with an external counsel.
# Quality of service we want to offer - are there any reasons to stop providing support in Romanian? Do we want to provide support in English by default at the cost of smooth customer experience?

Taking into the account issues described by me above I would like to get a clear confirmation that we see a business case in providing support in English by default before we spend resources on clarifying local legislation.

Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;

* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

h3. *Romanian Companies Law (Law No. 31/1990):*

*  This article covers the legal effects of mergers and splits, specifically how assets, liabilities, rights, and obligations are transferred to the resulting or absorbing entity.
* *Text of Article 238*:
"(1) The merger or division shall produce effects:
** a) In the case of mergers by absorption, from the date of the registration of the decision of the absorbing company with the Trade Register;
** b) In the case of mergers by formation of a new company or of a division by formation of new companies, from the date of the registration of the new company with the Trade Register. (2) *Upon the merger or division, the assets and liabilities of the absorbed or divided company shall be transferred entirely to the absorbing or new companies, as applicable.* (3) The companies resulting from the merger or division shall assume the rights and obligations of the absorbed or divided companies, as stipulated in the merger or division project."

h3. *Romanian Civil Code*:

* This article deals with the transfer of obligations through legal succession, which applies in cases of mergers or divisions.
* *Text of Article 2329*:
"In the case of universal succession or a merger, the successor or the absorbing legal entity takes over the rights and obligations of the entity that ceases to exist, *including those that have arisen before the merger took effect*, unless otherwise provided by law or by the parties."

Hi [~accountid:626c24971a4eb30069d28197] 

Finland’s reclass risk is not low – therefore there are suggestions which should be followed when implementing Bolt Rewards in Finland. Namely, some features of the program should not be used in Finland.

The suggestions are as follows:

# Ideally, Bolt Rewards would be offered to all drivers - this is the least risky approach and its effect on the reclass risk would be close to zero.
However, if that is not commercially viable then the scope of drivers that are able to participate in the program should be based on their +ride completion rate+ (e.g. complete 10 trips within a month and become part of Bolt Rewards program!). No other performance metrics of drivers should be considered when enabling them to use Bolt Rewards. Please also note that if completion rate is chosen, then the threshold of completed rides should not be a disproportionate and unrealistic number.
# Internal benefits are to be avoided. This includes the acceptance screen transparency feature (where only certain tier drivers can see the price and destination of the trip before acceptance). It is legal’s assessment that using such internal benefits would raise the reclass risk exponentially. Therefore it should be avoided as to not raise Finland’s risk level further.
# The third party offers as rewards should be low value offers such as mobile phone service vouchers, car washes, fuel cards, restaurant vouchers etc.
# When marketing and communicating with drivers about the program do not use terminology such as “loyalty program”, “loyalty level”, “loyalty points” etc.

Let me know if you have any questions.

[duration_prom_query|https://thanos.nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph?g0.expr=sum%20by%20(rule_name)%20(increase(nodejs%3AAlertingMonitor%3Aduration_prom_query_duration_ms%5B1h%5D))%20%2F%20sum%20by%20(rule_name)%20(increase(nodejs%3AAlertingMonitor%3Aduration_prom_query_total%5B1h%5D))&g0.tab=0&g0.stacked=0&g0.range_input=1h&g0.max_source_resolution=0s&g0.deduplicate=1&g0.partial_response=0&g0.store_matches=%5B%5D&g0.engine=prometheus&g0.analyze=0&g0.tenant=].

There are two alternatives that we can implement.

1️⃣ Easy one. Create a common rule based on the [duration_prom_query|https://thanos.nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph?g0.expr=sum%20by%20(rule_name)%20(increase(nodejs%3AAlertingMonitor%3Aduration_prom_query_duration_ms%5B1h%5D))%20%2F%20sum%20by%20(rule_name)%20(increase(nodejs%3AAlertingMonitor%3Aduration_prom_query_total%5B1h%5D))&g0.tab=0&g0.stacked=0&g0.range_input=1h&g0.max_source_resolution=0s&g0.deduplicate=1&g0.partial_response=0&g0.store_matches=%5B%5D&g0.engine=prometheus&g0.analyze=0&g0.tenant=] and send it to {{component-alerting}} owners if a rule takes more than 1m (or more) to run. Then, as the alerting owners, we would manually notify the original owners of the rule and ask them to optimize it.



2️⃣ More complex. Modify the code to measure the PromQL duration after determining the code owners. Right now, the duration measure takes place in the [PrometheusQuerierBaseStrategy|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/ec245ba5076753587a499b346fbc3242c8405932/src/foundation/monitoring/alerting_worker/main/service/data_queriers/prometheus/strategies/PrometheusQuerierBaseStrategy.ts#L16]. We have to change the code and move it to the [PrometheusQueryExecutor|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/6db3b2ecc573f0f78334a2e5e1fa8f6dec20ca49/src/foundation/monitoring/alerting_worker/main/service/data_queriers/prometheus/PrometheusQueryExecutor.ts#L51], after the: {{this.setCodeOwnerOnResult(ctx, node, data);}} We also need to change the [promQueryDurations|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/6aadee602176bc76669770c50ab58b9ebe2bbebf/common/alerting/AlertingMonitor.ts#L86] to account for the code owner. Then, we’d create a rule over this measure and automatically notify the owners if the duration exceeds a defined threshold.

IMO, the code is nicely structured, and I wouldn’t change it. But let’s see if this is a must.

I’ve looked again, trying to identify potential issues that caused the increase in response time for “/internal/findProvidersInUserRangeV2” endpoint. Since, we excluded that the increase is related to any change on our side, I’ve checked the endpoints that {{delivery-eater-data-store}} uses when computing the response for a call to {{findProvidersInUserRangeV2}}. My investigation showed a couple of things:

* Due to a recent change in platform side ([https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C5SQB8V6G/p1727680815305389|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C5SQB8V6G/p1727680815305389|smart-link] ), nodemonitor now has data only for the last 40 days, so for anything older than that we need to directly query Thanos ([thanos.nodemonitor.boltint.net|http://thanos.nodemonitor.boltint.net/]) which adds an extra layer of complexity to such investigations
* As such, I would strongly recommend that in the future, such investigations should have a higher priority, and we should try to conclude them in the 40 days window that still has data.
* Going further, I’ve looked at all major endpoints that {{"/internal/findProvidersInUserRangeV2"}} calls (you can see it below), and to me, the only possible lead is that there was a small increase in duration for {{/internal/areProvidersAvailable"}} from {{delivery-provider}} (around the date of 14th of June). So, given, that all other endpoints seemed to display no significant change in latency during that period, I would argue that  {{/internal/areProvidersAvailable}} increase might be the culprit for our issue.

The main bottleneck is the {{/internal/distanceMatrixTable}} endpoint of {{geo-routing}} / {{geo-osrm-car}}.

The solution employed is twofold:

1) Parallelise calls to {{/internal/distanceMatrixTable}} to avoid timeouts.

2) Make {{/internal/distanceMatrixTable}} endpoint faster by dropping Protobuf and making response more compact - return actual numeric distance / duration matrices to have less JSON characters.

Perf tests were performed for {{/internal/distanceMatrixTable}} in prelive using input matrices of size 300 x 1000.

*Scenario 1: PBF encoding between* {{geo-osrm-car}} *and* {{geo-routing}}*:*

{noformat}p50:4500ms	p95:5800ms	p99:6600ms{noformat}

“EBADF: bad file descriptor, read” error is happening because when we update the database file, we switch the database reader to use the new file and then close the connection to the old file (Closing of connection is required because otherwise there is memory leak: the file doesn’t get deleted). In between, we still have some requests that are using an old database reader. 

Based on my initial observation, I thought of a potential fix to use some locking mechanism while switching the database to the new version. But currently, NJSC doesn’t have a {{read-write}} locking mechanism available. 

Then I asked the [question|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C049U1GKWQN/p1729774282343129] in PINT support and we found a solution that uses counter and closes the connection when the reader is abandoned and no longer in use.

Please see below legal requirements for electronic employment contract signing:

# *Romania* 

On 8 July 2024, Romania published and adopted Law no. 214/2024 on electronic signature and trust which entered into force on 8 October 2024. Expanding on the EU Regulation on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions (eIDAS Regulation), the new Law makes several types of electronic signatures similar to handwritten signatures. For Employment agreements, an electronic document fulfils this requirement *if signed with a qualified or advanced electronic signature*, which are deemed equivalent to handwritten signatures.

Employers may use +a simple electronic signature+ for some less important / internal employment-related documents, such as certificates, forms, expense reports etc, subject to any conditions set in their internal regulations. 

# *Croatia*

The Ministry of Economy, Employment and Entrepreneurship of Croatia issued an official opinion that an employment contract that is concluded electronically *and signed with a qualified electronic signature*, is considered to be in writing in compliance with the _Employment Act_.

# *Switzerland*

Under Swiss law, an employment contract under private law can generally be concluded without any formalities. This means that any type of contract conclusion is eligible - and thus any type of digital signature (QES; FES; simple digital signature; digitally copied signature) is also suitable for concluding the contract. 

However, there are weighty exceptions. The law (Swiss Code of Obligations) has formal requirements for certain agreements that are usually included in employment contracts. For example, it must be agreed in writing that overtime worked will not be paid or compensated separately. Similarly, a post-contractual non-competition clause, for example, must be agreed in writing. In addition, collective employment agreements regularly provide that provisions contained therein may only be deviated from in writing. 

Written form within the meaning of the law requires a handwritten signature. Alternatively, *only so-called qualified electronic signatures* are permitted in accordance with the Federal Electronic Signature Act of March 18, 2016 (QES). 

 A signature with a digital signature that does not meet the requirements for a qualified electronic signature is therefore not sufficient for the legal validity of the aforementioned clauses. In other words, the use of advanced electronic signatures (FES) or simple electronic signatures (e.g. standard DocuSign solution) is not sufficient. Nor, of course, are digitally copied signatures sufficient. The use of such insufficient digital signatures leads to an employment contract being valid in principle, but the contract may contain provisions that have not been validly agreed and are therefore not enforceable (partial invalidity due to lack of form).

*Conclusion:* It's advisable to confirm whether Box Sign and HelloSign can provide *qualified electronic signature* in these jurisdictions or *advanced electronic signature in Romania.* Easiest way would be to contact our contact person in Box Sign and HelloSign and clarify these questions directly with them as I am not familiar with the specifics of services they are providing to us.

h2. *Using OpenAI Model*

*Labelling jobs:* 

We have used internal human force to label tickets, with as much diversity as we could muster through internal volunteers. Datasets and labels followed the instructions requested in this ticket, by the Privacy team. Labelling jobs have been finished.



*Experiments:* 

The current system has been tested live on specific markets, but without making any decisions, since we have been experimenting with accuracy levels. Cross-checking AI detection with Human detection and then having a further human analysis - [*Example*|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C07QRMEDDKK/p1730108895540699]



*Current Focus*

Intention Labelling was built to detect several intentions: Aggressive/Violent Harassment,	Sexual Harassment, Impersonation, Offline Trip Negotiation, Account Phishing, and Price Negotiation. However since the advent of this project, we’ve been noticing a steep increase in fraudulent activities through our communication channels, so we are increasing our attention on Account Phishing and expanding our detection to Defrauding. We will resume our efforts on optimising the remaining detections after the system is up to protect users against these fraudulent schemes.



*Current Status*

The current prompt with OpenAI has high enough accuracy - less than 5% False Positives and detection of 77% of true Account Phishing cases. We will keep improving these numbers as we move forward.

We are currently finalising the implementation for an action to happen when these fraudulent intentions are detected.



*Action:*

For Account Phishing and Defrauding our goal will be to shut down the Chat service conversation between the 2 involved users during that order, protecting the victim from continuous social Engineering techniques which may lead them to share their personal data. This block will happen only during the order where Account Phishing / Defrauding is detected. The full service will be restored on the next order.

At this stage, we will only take action on Account Phishing / Defrauding intentions

Actions for each detection will be documented on[ *Chat Intention Labelling - Actions*|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-jdIAKxCydW3ZI3sEYDA1HhP0PwTp4_zoFEUapd-QtE/edit?gid=0#gid=0]



*Launch*

We plan to roll out live tests with real-time detection and action as described above from the 4th of November. Tests will be rolled out in countries with high incidences of fraudulent activity. We will start tests in Cyprus and we follow the incidence order: CY, MT, CH, HR, PL, FR, NL, SK, BE, DE, Global.

* Check if the payment method used to make the order is not a business account. In this case, the refund will be sent to the business account balance.
* Check if the user did not spend their refund on a next order (or orders) for Bolt balance refunds
* Check if the user did not have a previous debt or previous failed payment that was covered up with the refund
* If refund was sent to Balance instead of card, check first if payment was made from card. Usually, if card payment fails, card refund also fails. Sometimes refund will be sent to balance in cases payment was charged from balance first as debt and the refund will clear the debt previously created by the balance charge. 
* Check [payment page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/payments/1946767063], to ensure there are no errors on the refund and advise the user to check with their bank if card refund was successfully completed.
** If there is an error, escalate to Commerce > Ride Hailing/Food/Rentals payments
* Only successful card payments can be refunded to card.

Dear Андрій,

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 7 October 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties (including the rights of passengers). Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled, in particular your order history between 30 September 2024 and 6 October 2024, which should contain the information that you have requested. We would like to point out that you can obtain your monthly total number of rides through the Bolt Driver Portal - Simply navigate to "My trips," specify the desired month, and the system will display the relevant data. To the extent that you require any additional information, we would be grateful if you could please specify (for example, clarification on what is meant by “total number within the radius”) so that our team can investigate.

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our privacy notice available at [https://bolt.eu/uk-ua/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/uk-ua/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

Since the driver’s position is part of the data tied to the service I received, it qualifies as personal data related to my ride. GDPR does not prohibit sharing such data when requested by the data subject (myself)_”), *I do not fully agree with the rider’s logic* - just because it is personal data related to their ride does not necessarily mean it is _their_ personal data. IMO, the data being requested is more the driver’s than it is the rider’s (particularly given that the rider was not in the car at the time).
* The amount of money being requested here is small, and so I would prioritise trying to refund the rider in the first instance, as this would likely kill off their cause of complaint.

*** (b) can we refund the rider the trip fee?
** (2) If so, write back to the rider saying: 
*** (a) data protection law entitles them to their personal data but not that of others, and we are always required to balance their rights against the rights of other individuals; and 
*** (b) we have refunded the trip fee.
** (3) If we cannot refund the trip, then given that this is a ‘grey area’ in terms of being technically both the driver’s and the rider’s personal data, and given that the data is very low risk, IMO we can provide the driver’s arrival location (and nothing else) to the rider in this case.

This issue originated from a temporary *single shard* deployment in the live environment, which led to messages on a single Event Buffer topic being encoded with two different schema versions. While this is an isolated incident, it had a significant impact on the end-to-end Event Buffer pipeline. Furthermore, rolling back the deployed shard did not resolve the issue.

Essentially, the clients (event buffer producers) do not handle schema versions directly; instead, they download and cache the latest version from the registry. In this scenario, we have two service domains:

* All shards, except for Ukraine, are operating with V1.
* The Ukraine shard is functioning with V2.

h3. What Happened

A non-Ukraine shard instance was initiated (due to k8s autoscaling), and subsequently, it began to use *V2 instead of V1*.

h3. Why

This situation is a potential race condition, as explained in the description.

h3. To Summarize

* Publishing two schema versions of messages to the same topic is *highly discouraged*, and the domain team should take steps to prevent this.
* Implementing automatic prevention at deployment time is a significant investment 👉. We should block deployments if we detect a single shard and the deployment includes an AVRO schema version that differs from the currently deployed one.
* We should ensure that an instance utilizes its own AVRO schema version and is not affected by a temporary instance that has published a different version.

This latter investment is estimated to take less than a week and should be worthwhile, even though the bug's occurrence is quite rare.

The answer is yes. The [Saudi Arabia Driver T&Cs|https://bolt.eu/en-sa/legal/tnc-drivers/?category=rides] cover reducing or canceling the driver fare with the following clauses:

* _4.10. Bolt Saudi Arabia may adjust the Fare for a particular order completed if we detect a violation (such as taking a longer route or not stopping the fare meter of Bolt App after Transportation Services have been completed) or in case a technical error affecting the final Fare is identified._ +*_Bolt Saudi Arabia may also reduce or cancel the Fare in case we have reasonable cause to suspect fraud_*+ _or a complaint by the Passenger indicates a violation by you. Bolt Saudi Arabia will only exercise its right to reduce or cancel the Fare in a reasonable and justified manner._
* Clauses 6.4 and 6.5 in particular give Bolt the right to cancel promo codes and withhold Tips in case of fraud.
* Furthermore, clause 6.9 gives Bolt the general right to set off fees against other financial obligations the driver has.

We do not have a particular clause in the T&Cs that mention the right to temporarily +withhold the driver earnings for 36h+. However, pursuant to clause 13.4:

“_We may also immediately suspend (block) your access to Bolt Platform and to Bolt Driver Account for the period of investigation if we suspect an infringement of the Agreement or fraudulent activity on your behalf. The block of access will be removed once the investigation disproves such suspicions._” 

This means we have a general right of blocking access to the services during an investigation; and this should also cover temporarily withholding funds for an investigation. It can also be argued that since we have the right to reduce fares in case of fraud (as written above), then it goes without saying that we would first need to investigate the fraud for a reasonable time before deciding if the fare is reduced or not.

In conclusion, there are no legal blocks in the T&Cs.

Hi [~accountid:712020:02902587-2e99-4b83-bff4-2a998b3acbf8], [~accountid:712020:36a81a2e-25b2-4001-b97a-448ab17ddb11], please find the local assessment of launching DQO as well as linking Blast Dispatch to DQO below. 

+Launch of DQO+

* Local teams/Public Policy must be aware of that *DQO is a ‘high risk feature’/‘high impact feature’* that is likely to escalate reclassification risk in any market. 
* We should *expect to have to disclose the existence of DQO* as part of any reclassification claims (e.g. during any court proceedings when asked about our operating model), regulatory enquiries or via the transparency obligations of the Platform Work Directive. 
* To avoid 'dramatically increasing risk', DQO can be launched as a *_simultaneous replacement_* to acceptance rate blocking (‘ARB’). This means that we cannot use both ARB and DQO as these are both high risk features (meaning that any cities in Sweden still having ARB *cannot* also have DQO). 
* *Before launching* DQO, also Public Policy needs to approve of the launch[~accountid:712020:36cbea54-0723-40fc-a8d1-2d4945acece1][~accountid:5eb133e4ad226b0ba40fc75d] please inform if enabling this feature imposes a blocker from your point of view. 
* *Privacy* ([~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd]) will need to decide whether we need to amend the privacy notice for the market to facilitate the launch of DQO (which I believe has already been done [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C051K1C57KJ/p1729865712210749?thread_ts=1729007547.285459&cid=C051K1C57KJ], but let me know if not). 

+Linking Blast Dispatch to DQO+ 

* When basing dispatching on DQO, this would mean that specific performance metrics are linked into the dispatching logic. This is therefore considered as a risky feature from a reclass point of view ('_allocation of work based on performance'_). 
* However, *linking the DQO to the Blast Dispatch* (if DQO has been rolled-out) won’t increase the risk level of the market as turning on the DQO already increased the risk significantly (if this is accepted by all stakeholders). 
* Note that *the dispatching logic is subject to disclosure* in the event of legal proceedings or an authority request. The dispatching logic must also *be reflected in the privacy notice* if personal data of the drivers are processed for this purpose (to be confirmed by [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd]). 
* Public Policy needs to confirm if they see any blockers from their point of view ([~accountid:712020:36cbea54-0723-40fc-a8d1-2d4945acece1], [~accountid:5eb133e4ad226b0ba40fc75d]).

*To summarize*, launching DQO as well as linking Blast Dispatch to DQO is high risk and given this then local teams must be aware of the potential negative impact this could cause, as well as both Public Policy and Privacy giving their go-ahead for launch.

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

Yours sincerely,



Bolt

+*Calculation to see outstanding amount at end of the month*+

Hi [~accountid:712020:7f47c2af-14e1-4206-a795-ac87cb906276], to chime in here - price discrimination based on a persons nationality or place of residence is forbidden in the EU.

So called “Tourist Pricing“ has been discussed a number of times in other markets (i.e. charging a higher rate to non-nationals). Irrespective of how it is portrayed, so called tourist pricing looks and feels like the above mentioned price discrimination to both our users and to consumer protection authorities, hence we’ve consistently advised Product, regional and local operations that it is high risk and should not be done. 

Targeted campaigns are of course permitted (e.g. for students, new users etc). In my view, a targeted campaign for a subset of users that commute regularly in a particular city is okay. The language used both internally and externally should be consistent however: Bolt is offering a discount campaign targeted at regular commuters, not one that excludes tourists. 

Best, LC

How does search work?

When you search for restaurants or grocery providers, you'll see a list of providers, each with a carousel of items underneath. Providers are ranked based on several factors to ensure the most relevant results are shown first:

# *Partner Availability*
#* Providers available for delivery appear at the top.
#* Next, you'll see providers offering pick-up but not delivery.
#* Providers currently unavailable are listed last.
# *Matching Name or Menu Items*
#* Partners whose names and menu items start with your search query are ranked higher.
# *Name Matches*
#* Partners whose names begin with your search query.
# *Menu Item Matches*
#* Partners with menu items that match your search query.
# *Distance*
#* Providers closest to your location are ranked higher.

Under each provider, the items carousel prioritizes items that match your search query, ranked by how well they match. The remaining spaces are filled with the provider’s popular items.

You can also apply filters to refine your search further. When filters are applied, the results and rankings will adjust to match your preferences.

AI module and our IoT are part of a product and they can’t be used outside the scooter as an individual product. Thus these are UL certified together with the main product which is the scooter. 

UL standard that applies to scooters is UL2272. This says that there are special requirements (in AI module context) for

* The plastic enclosure material: flammability and material strength. Protection from electrical and mechanical hazards
* Wiring and it insulation: flammabilty, cable routing safety, 
* Electrical separation: proper insulation for proper voltage
** UL 60950-1
* Vibration test according to EN 60068-2-64
* Water ingress: IPx4





Currently our scooter is being verified by the UL. In the context of our IoT we have provided info about its

* Cabling (Higo)
* PCB (HX)
* Connectors (Higo)
* [(check further here)|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cyKcM0WBSH4KDCFx7zirI6QNsnuP8EU5/edit]

[~accountid:712020:64b64810-17ee-4eae-a1d9-0887a9baa408] [~accountid:712020:12ec6339-bd3a-42a1-a64d-dc9e914d0db6], thanks for the syncs earlier today! I have looked into this again to find an alternative approach, please find my assessment below: 

+General approach+

* As mentioned before, it would be better to provide gift cards directly to the fleets, which could then distribute them to their drivers. 
* Also, if drivers are already employed by the fleets (who gives these out), the risk of us being classified as employers is generally much lower than if gift cards are provided directly to independent drivers.

+Alternative approach+

* If the general approach creates an administrative burden, *an alternative* could be to *obtain the fleet’s consent* to provide gift cards to its drivers. 
** We could collect this consent through a survey where Bolt explains the initiative, emphasizes that the fleet is our direct partner, and asks for the fleet’s consent to offer gift cards to drivers for they go at a specific store. Fleets could respond with "Yes" or "No." 
** Additionally, the fleet could provide a list of drivers eligible to receive a gift card (e.g. all drivers that brand the fleets’ car or similar). This way, the fleet has full information and the final say (control over the benefit given to its drivers).

+Comms in relation to this initiative+

* The comms from our side are *only for the fleets and not to be directly communicated to the drivers*. 
* It might however be helpful if the fleets send some communication directly to their drivers explaining this initiative and that the certificate can be received at the specific shop. By doing this, the fleets will act as employers and demonstrate that they have a say in this bonus.
* In our comms to the fleet, we should also mention these details about the third party distributing the certificates and ask for their consent regarding this (i.e. consent only from the fleet that the certificates will be distributed to its drivers by the third party (name it also so it’s clear for the fleet)).

[Here|https://bolt-incentives.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/3022622012364763?o=2472566184436351#command/3151012526370366] I had a quick look at the relations between surge&ride distance, and surge&number of orders:
- A moderate linear relationship exists for some cities in case of surge and order distance.
- In the case of a number of orders and surge - only 3 cities have a moderate linear relationship between these 2.

[There is a query|https://bolt-incentives.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/3022622012364763?o=2472566184436351#command/3151012526370108] for surge (avg_multiplier) and Base price index (bpi): 

* Base price indexes are on a daily level, not weekly. The reason is that we want them to reflect time-based pricing which won’t be that noticeable on the weekly scale.
* There are several multiplier types: supply_demand (when we try to make them even and get equilibrium on the marketplace), and RVP (ride value pricing) - when we know that trip is not great and probably won’t be accepted, we try to get the price higher to match the rider with a driver still. I think for us it doesn’t matter what type is it, it’s a multiplier affecting the ride price. Hence. I kept the query blind to the multiplier types.

Hey [~accountid:712020:6dc45e6d-eb79-499c-ae48-08d3e5c22b23], there are three scenarios here.

First scenario - the employment of minors. Generally, minors can enter into employment agreements from 16 years old, and after that, we can engage them as employees of the fleet. At the same time, we would still need to require parental consent for accepting our T&Cs by such a minor.

Second scenario - registration of a minor as an individual entrepreneur. Starting from 16 years old, with the submission of parental consent the minor can register as an individual entrepreneur. In this case, from the time of such registration, they gain full legal capacity and we can engage them with no further docs.

Third scenario - engaging the minor on the basis of just a civil law agreement (our T&Cs). The minors in the age of 14-18 can enter into civil law agreements with the parental consent. However, for using the funds that they would receive as payment from us to their bank accounts, some banks might require the consent of parents and the guardianship and care authority (_орган опіки та піклування_), as well as other relevant docs (copy of our T&Cs, etc.). This is a matter of interpretation of the laws and instructions by each bank and difficult to predict whether such a minor could then freely use the money. 

Generally, the second scenario is the most optimal and feasible if we have a way to make payments to the bank accounts of the individual entrepreneurs.

Please let me know if you have more questions here.

* Driver Terms

We will confirm to you in writing when this is the case save where we are unable or are advised not to do so for regulatory or legal reasons. * _Fraud Policy:_
