The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount. 


Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Cheers,
Marten

_Dzień dobry,_

_odwołanie się w utd do przestępstw przeciwko zdrowiu i życiu oraz przeciwko wolności seksualnej i obyczajności nie jest zawężone wyłącznie do przepisów KK._

_II. Pozakodeksowe – przykłady:_

* _art. 58 ustawy o zawodach lekarza i lekarza dentysty_
* _Art. 30 i art. 31 ustawy o publicznej służbie krwi_
* _Art. 71 ust 2 ustawy o diagnostyce laboratoryjnej_
* _Art. 91 – 103 ustawy o wyrobach medycznych_
* _art. 85 i 86 ustawy o zawodach pielęgniarki i położnej_
* _art. 53 ustawy o ochronie zdrowia psychicznego_
* _art. 124 – 126 c ustawy prawo farmaceutyczne_
* _art. 43 ustawy o wychowaniu w trzeźwości i przeciwdziałaniu alkoholizmowi_

_Pełen katalog przestępstw będzie bardzo ciężki do przygotowania, nie tylko ze względu na to, że nie znam wszystkich ustaw szczegółowych, w których może pojawić się jakiś przepis karny chroniący w/w dobra, ale również i z tego względu, że w przypadku przestępstw przeciwko zdrowiu przedmiotem ochrony może być zarówno dobro o charakterze indywidualnym (i raczej taki typ przestępstwa należałoby zaliczać do katalogu), jak i dobro o charakterze zbiorowym. # *Liability for Inaccessibility*

To add clarity around access-related charges, we’re happy to propose the following language:

“The Client shall not be liable for any rent, service charges, or taxes for any period during which the Client is unable to access or use the Unit, provided that such lack of access is not due to the Client’s own actions, negligence, or failure to comply with the terms of this Agreement.”

This ensures that only access disruptions beyond the Client’s control would qualify for a waiver of charges.

 

# *Mutual Exclusion of Indirect/Consequential Losses (Clause 7.2)*

After careful review, we feel that keeping Clause 7.2 as a unilateral exclusion remains consistent with industry standards and fairly distributes risk. Given the Provider’s ongoing operational responsibilities, this arrangement helps us manage potential liabilities effectively. We do recommend arranging insurance to cover any potential indirect losses as a precaution, as outlined in the clause.

 

# *Mutual Termination for Cause (Clause 1.5)*

We’re open to adjusting this clause so that both parties have equal rights to terminate the agreement for specific situations, such as insolvency or a material breach that isn’t remedied within a reasonable timeframe. The proposed amendment would read:

“Either party may terminate this agreement if the other party is in material breach of any obligation hereunder and fails to remedy such breach within fourteen (14) days of receiving written notice of the breach.”

This gives both sides a clear course of action in serious cases while keeping protections balanced.

 

# *Late Payment Fees*

On this point, we’d like to keep the current late payment fee structure, which includes a daily late fee of 0.25% (capped at 50% of the outstanding amount). These terms are in place to reflect the real costs of managing overdue payments, and we believe they help support smooth operations overall.

 

*Conclusion*

We hope these responses provide the clarity and balance you’re looking for. Our aim is to ensure this agreement works well for both sides, and we’re looking forward to finalising terms together. Please let us know if there’s anything more, you’d like to discuss.

I’ve compared the wording with the Romanian version (with the help of Google translate), and the clauses are worded slightly differently. Please see: 



English version 

{quote}Art. 4. The total monthly rent for this rental contract is 3292.80 EURO plus VAT, representing 4.90 EUR/sqm plus VAT and the security insurance is ........... plus VAT plus the value of the utilities mentioned in art.2 according to the records on the measuring devices related to the space.{quote}



Romanian version (translated to English with the help of Google) 

{quote}Art. 4. The total monthly rent related to this rental agreement is of 3292.80 EURO to which VAT is added, representing 4.90 EUR/sqm plus VAT, to which add the value of the utilities mentioned in art. 2 according to the records on the devices as related to the space.{quote}



The part about “security insurance” has been omitted from the Romanian version. So I would say that the first thing we need to do is to check which version are we going to follow, and then make sure that both versions of the agreement will stipulate the same thing before signing (also, considering that there’s a discrepancy in Art 4, I think it would be best to have the whole agreement cross-checked for discrepancies). 

Now, when it comes to this “security insurance” part specifically - this is not a well-known / commonly used term in practice. With the lack of further context, it is hard to tell what is specifically meant here. However, if I were to venture a guess - it seems to me that the landlord has this clause in their contract template because sometimes the landlord agrees with its tenants that the landlord will purchase insurance on behalf of the tenant, and then the tenant will compensate the cost of insurance. 

However, currently, it’s unclear to me whether we have made such an agreement with the landlord or not. 

Regardless, all our scooter warehouses are covered with a group liability insurance - meaning that any damage that we have caused we are liable for, will be compensated to the landlord by our insurance. Our insurance does not cover any other risks to the property (flooding, fire, theft, vandalism, etc.) - because that is not an “insurable interest“ for us. If the landlord is trying to push insurance on us that is overlapping with the cover that we already have from our group policy, I would suggest pushing back on this. 



In short, 

* let’s make sure which version of the contract we need to follow - the English or Romanian 
* let’s make sure that both versions will be aligned
* let’s check with the landlord what is meant by “security insurance” and why no sum has been mentioned there.

It was found that IOT ZK201 was misreporting the battery SN:

The issue pertains to a discrepancy in how the ZK200 is reading the battery BMS serial numbers compared to the ZK115MGC devices. Below are the details:

* *Working Device*: ZK115MGC (Protocol Version: EF8046)
* When connected to a battery, this version reads the correct BMS serial number: *0016010700000255*.

* *Issue with ZK200*: (Protocol Version: OK043A)
* When I connect the same battery to the ZK200, it returns an incorrect serial number: *0016010700000055*.

After some investigation, Okai found the issue in FW 1056, and they will distribute a new FW version 1064 to solve the SN report.

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer.

1️⃣ I had 3 shadowing sessions (IH Rides, IH Delivery, and OS Rides to see how Beehive playmode works), and these are the changes I made based on my observations:

* Added [+a step+|https://www.figma.com/board/Z7dTZTQtFBHLOg1fOm8cxE/Non-safety-ticket-handling-process?node-id=277-1146&t=CaQfzdWY2GOFQDdd-4] to communicate to the customer that the issue is resolved in another ticket in the duplicate tickets process;
* Added [+a whole new process+|https://www.figma.com/board/Z7dTZTQtFBHLOg1fOm8cxE/Non-safety-ticket-handling-process?node-id=277-842&t=CaQfzdWY2GOFQDdd-4] for checking Linked cases. I also added [+additional note here+|https://www.figma.com/board/Z7dTZTQtFBHLOg1fOm8cxE/Non-safety-ticket-handling-process?node-id=196-996&t=CaQfzdWY2GOFQDdd-4] that asks the agent to leave internal notes in another linked ticket if it's handled by someone else;
* Moved the [+adding issue tags step+|https://www.figma.com/board/Z7dTZTQtFBHLOg1fOm8cxE/Non-safety-ticket-handling-process?node-id=299-885&t=CaQfzdWY2GOFQDdd-4] to the beginning, and I also mentioned in [+the note+|https://www.figma.com/board/Z7dTZTQtFBHLOg1fOm8cxE/Non-safety-ticket-handling-process?node-id=277-1466&t=CaQfzdWY2GOFQDdd-4] that issue tags should be added as soon as CS understands what the issue is about. There is also [+a step in the end+|https://www.figma.com/board/Z7dTZTQtFBHLOg1fOm8cxE/Non-safety-ticket-handling-process?node-id=26-207&t=CaQfzdWY2GOFQDdd-4] that asks the agent to check if all the issue tags are added before closing the ticket.
* Changed the wording from "close the ticket" to "put the ticket on pending" [+here+|https://www.figma.com/board/Z7dTZTQtFBHLOg1fOm8cxE/Non-safety-ticket-handling-process?node-id=36-1056&t=CaQfzdWY2GOFQDdd-4], so the customer doesn't get "Does this solve your issue?" question again and the ticket doesn't get reopened for the nth time.

2️⃣ I finished the [+optimized map+|https://www.figma.com/board/Z7dTZTQtFBHLOg1fOm8cxE/Non-safety-ticket-handling-process?node-id=203-1420&t=CaQfzdWY2GOFQDdd-4] for [+Information about automatic compensations+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/13270?country=global&language=en]:

* I had to keep a rule for Delivery that if automation offered a full refund for just a missing/wrong item in the menu, the agents should not offer a full refund but to calculate the value of the missing item and offer it instead - I discussed this with [@himanshu.narvekar|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U057S9XMFV1] and that was his comment "*_There is no reason to refund the whole order if only 1 drink was missing from the order. Hi [~accountid:5d288a402c5a110c1d4775b5] - thanks for escalating this. I have reviewed it and, in short, this does not qualify as a personal data incident and is not necessarily something that Bolt can control / resolve for the rider. There are some minor mitigation steps that we _could_ take, but this depends on a few clarifications. 

I therefore include below some questions, and an explanation of our position on this from a Privacy POV. I will repeat the headline points in the Slack channel.

*QUESTIONS*

# I assume that the customer information that the drivers are sharing on the WhatsApp group is information that is ordinarily available to the driver via their Bolt app / Driver Portal (i.e., the drivers did not come into possession of such information through some _fault_ in Bolt’s systems)?
# Are we able to identify any of the drivers that are sharing this information on the WhatsApp group? I assume not based on the information provided, but just to check.

*ANALYSIS*

* If the information that the drivers are sharing should not have been accessible to the drivers in the first place (e.g., it was the result of a cybersecurity leak), then this would count as a personal data breach that we would need to address.
* However (as appears to be the case here), if the drivers are ordinarily able to access this data through the Bolt app, then it is no fault of Bolt’s that the drivers are sharing this information via private WhatsApp channels. 
* Regardless of the fact that the information that the drivers are sharing on the WhatsApp group is taken from the Bolt app, the drivers are *independent data controllers* with respect to this information. As such, it is up to the drivers what they do with this information, as well as to assess whether they are acting in line with applicable privacy laws. This is something Bolt has no control over.
* Beyond asking the relevant drivers to refrain from sharing this information (as well as checking whether sharing it violates any of Bolt’s T&Cs and taking appropriate action in response), there is therefore not much we can do here from a Privacy POV - Bolt is not under a privacy obligation to act here, and there is not much we can do to stop it in any event.

*NEXT STEPS*

* {color:#36b37e}*If we are able to locate any of the drivers*{color} who have been sharing this information on the WhatsApp channel, you should first check with the local legal team whether there are any grounds in Bolt’s T&Cs for taking action against the drivers (e.g., suspending account access) on the basis of sharing passenger information in this way - please let me know what they say either way. Assuming that there is not much we can do here, I would then suggest taking the following steps:
** (1) Write to the drivers with the following message:
*** _“Hello,_
_We are reaching out to you to inform you that a concerned passenger contacted us about you uploading passenger information onto a group WhatsApp channel._
_While we do not control what you upload to messaging services, we kindly request you to take into account that laws protecting personal data, including the EU GDPR, apply to you when you process, use, collect and share personal data, especially when your actions cause distress to the passengers.”_
** (2) Write to the rider with the following message:
*** “_Hello,_
_We would like to inform you that we reached out to the drivers and requested for the information to be removed from the WhatsApp channel._
_However, since drivers are independent service providers, and therefore they are independent data controllers with respect to the information being shared in this case, it is up to them to assess whether they are acting in line with applicable data protection laws, as Bolt has no control over it_.”
* {color:#ff5630}*If we cannot locate any of the drivers*{color} who have been sharing this information on the WhatsApp channel, then we could consider writing to the rider with the following:
** “_Hello,_
_Thank you for bringing this matter to our attention._
_Bolt takes the privacy of its users seriously. However, please note that since drivers are independent service providers, and therefore independent data controllers with respect to the information being shared in this case, it is up to the drivers to assess whether they are acting in line with applicable data protection laws. Unfortunately, Bolt has no control over this issue_.”

*Solution for Card migration*

Main idea:

* We should receive updated values for {{card}} payment instruments
* We ask Payments team to send events with new values via existing {{"payment-instrument"}} MQ topic. Note: we listen only to {{active}} statuses

Solution:

We have 2 subscribers for {{"payment-instrument"}} MQ events:

* in {{fraud-payment-data-sync}} for storing instruments into {{user_card_alias}} table
* in {{fraud-graph-data-sync}} for adding user relations

* {{user_card_alias}} *table*

* We continue listening to events. We need to add new {{card}} payment instrument rows in table and keep existing {{processout}} rows
* There is {{UNIQUE INDEX `...` (`user_id` ASC, `card_alias` ASC)}} which doesn’t allow to store new and keep existing rows in the same time
* We should drop UNIQUE constraint
** Asked #dev-db-support [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CNKLBL33P/p1730364589157959|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CNKLBL33P/p1730364589157959|smart-link] 
** {{CREATE INDEX 'my_index_2' ON my_table (a, b)}}  - create another non-unique index for the same columns
** {{DROP INDEX 'my_index' ON my_table}} - drop unique index
* What about potential duplicates after dropping unique index?
** Replace current {{upsertCardAlias}} approach with following
** SELECT existing rows by user_id and card_alias
** If there are no rows => insert new row
** If there are rows
*** Compare new entity with existing rows by: user_id, card_alias, payment_method_id, payment_method_type
*** Skip new entity if it has same values for above 4 fields as existing rows
*** Add new entity if it has different values for payment_method_id, payment_method_type
*** Technically, new uniqueness constraint would be (user_id, card_alias, payment_method_id, payment_method_type), but it will be checked during INSERTs into table. 
We won’t add this constraint as index to not avoid table size increase

*user relations*

Same as for PayPal. We don’t need to do any updates since we use card alias (aka fingerprint) for relations

{noformat}  INDEX `delete_after_status_idx` (`delete_after` ASC, `status` ASC),{noformat}

{noformat}id|select_type|table|partitions|type |possible_keys          |key                    |key_len|ref|rows  |filtered|Extra                   |

 1|SIMPLE     |frsdd|          |range|delete_after_status_idx|delete_after_status_idx|4      |   |337745|    25.0|Using where; Using index|{noformat}

A more efficient index would be

{noformat}INDEX `delete_after_status_idx` (`status` ASC, `delete_after` ASC),{noformat}

where the {{status}} column goes first.{quote}

Even though iteration over the B-Tree nodes cannot be avoided with this index (see [this comment|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/VERIFY-2367?focusedCommentId=2699383]), it’s still more efficient when {{status}} condition is more limiting than the {{data_after}} condition. Here’s an example:

{code:sql}SELECT COUNT(*) as count
FROM `flow_run_scheduled_data_deletion` AS frsdd
WHERE frsdd.status in ('done') AND frsdd.delete_after > FROM_UNIXTIME(1729791093){code}

There are {{1163015}} rows that satisfy the condition {{frsdd.delete_after > FROM_UNIXTIME(1729791093)}}, and only {{11180}} of them have {{done}} status.

The query execution time is {{0.217s}} when {{delete_after_status_idx}} index is used. We have to iterate over {{1163015}} B-Tree nodes ({{Handler_read_next}}).

{code:sql}SELECT COUNT(*) as count
FROM `flow_run_scheduled_data_deletion` AS frsdd FORCE INDEX (delete_after_status_idx)

If infringements are established, the Municipal Executive can suspend or withdraw the issued permit, after which the operator must remove all partial scooters within 45 hours.”_

I would need to instruct external counsel for a  precise analysis, but  BE law stems from and align with EU Directive on public procurement contracts. Accordingly the municipality might be entitled claim damages for the service disruption.

I took the example provided by [booking.com|http://booking.com/] where their commission is equal to ours (20%) showing that their commission needs to be lower that our commission charged to the driver. Otherwise we will not make money as we would need to pay [booking.com|http://booking.com/] commission and also bear the VAT cost of their commission (invoice issued to the traveller) with the impact on P&L.

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/15o3IzgvqfNjTjg4r7Z6WodyHlAS9ELptKQ-LrnVS984/edit?gid=0#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/15o3IzgvqfNjTjg4r7Z6WodyHlAS9ELptKQ-LrnVS984/edit?gid=0#gid=0|smart-link] 

* I took into the consideration 3 models: centralised, localised and UK
* based on the initial example with final price 100. We will pay 80 to the driver and 20 to booking. Additionally we would need to cover 3,61 of VAT on their booking fee, while we will get the commission from the driver equals to 16. In UK we will not have 3,61 VAT impact because of TOMS but we couldn’t deduct VAT from [booking.com|http://booking.com/] commission invoice (in our example 4)
* If the decision is to go with the deal, we would need to be extremely careful with UK due to 2 court cases which we have (TOMS and employment) and planned agency model implementation out of London and definitely not to start with this market as a pilot. Any action in UK would need throughout legal analysis.
* I have talked with TP and the desirable set-up would be to have separate invoice to Bolt Ops for centralised markets and separate invoices for localised markets (and UK)
* It would be more desirable from tax PoV to have [booking.com|http://booking.com/] commission charged to the traveller on one the ride invoice:

ride price: 80
booking fee: 20
VAT (if needed split by two rates)
total

* we analysed the situation where travellers are individuals (B2C) we shall be able to ensure that no B2B is allowed. I mean business customers may be travellers but we will not obliged ourselves to issue valid B2B invoice due to much more complex regulations and e-invoicing requirements. Something to raise to Legal. It would be extremely important if (for any reasons) we would issue two separate invoices to the traveller (one for the ride, second for booking fee) due to shifts in the place of taxation.
* I have not analysed partner markets.

To sum-up: there are no major tax stoppers to proceed with the deal. It is more about the calculation of the profitability of this deal vs tax costs and costs of the product development.
As discussed, we also need to ensure that we are not treated as passenger transportation provider but platform selling on another platform.

*I’ve checked the linked threads. I can summarize in two main concerns:*

* A link shortening tool for internal use (internal tools) - which is not what we are interested in.
* The tool being publicly accessible and not having governing rights (might create phishing links) - we can use CMS with limited access and only through a ticket.
* Usage of main domain - use of main domain is okay for as long us we don’t use mass SMS. (email is okay since we are already mentioning our domain in every email)

*What we need a is a simple way to:*

* Quickly “wrap” links into short links 
* Have the ability to document the link origin/use case/ requester/country.
* Link being really short (for QR use)
* Control/modify the target link 

*Currently:*
There is a lot of tickets coming in that request a short link or QR code. We don’t have a solution for web links. Appsflyer covers only app links / deep links (also no history/logs to track who requested).

*Proposal:*
*1.* Using _Strapi_, create a new collection type: “link” or “link redirects”. Don’t use “infra” on redirects. 

Have fields:

# Id (auto-incremented)
# Target link (required)
# Alias link (optional)
# Comment/requester
# Country
# UTM settings
# …
# Generated short link


The most important parts are *id* and *generated short link.* 
Once an entry is saved, run the *id* through hashid/sqids with a setting of alphanumeric small/large caps (62 characters, underscore and dash would add another 2) and minimum length limit of 3. This would give us ~250,000 possible combinations to fit into lenght of 3 characters. 

Now an *id* of 64 might give as an output of *w6y* as an example. We will use this for our short link. 

*2.* Create a route on gatsby or node:  [bolt.eu/go/|http://bolt.eu/go/] 

The server route will take in the slug (such as *w6y,* or https://_bolt.eu/go/w6y_ ). 
The app will make a request to CMS API and ask what should the redirect URL be for *w6y* (if it does not exist just re)
The app will respond with a header of 301 and redirect to the target URL. 
On app level we can introduce memory cache so that we don’t have to touch the database on each request.

No client / front-end needed.

Links like _https://bolt.eu/go/w6y_  can easily be wrapped into pretty QR codes.

Hi, everybody! I am coming to you with an update on how we communicate with accused users in regards to *safety incidents*

!1f447@2x.png|width=44,height=44,alt=":point_down:"!

*Context:*
We had some Safety Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), like the ones covering physical and sexual assault cases, where it was mentioned that we couldn’t share the allegation with the reported user. Together with CS Safety, Privacy and Legal teams, we have reviewed the guidelines for Eater and Courier Safety Events to make them compliant, more clear, and to make investigations more meaningful.*Update:*
Please see the [Delivery Safety Case Handling Workflow|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/90194?country=global&language=en] and the example templates which are available in the [safety event-specific SOPs|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4408525302418123?country=global&language=en]. I’ve outlined the main points of the update below:

!1f50d@2x.png|width=44,height=44,alt=":mag:"!

*Investigating the report*

* We should always inform the reported user about the suspension on their account;
* We should state that the report came from ‘a third party’, e.g ‘_we have received a report stating that’_ when reaching out to the reported user;
* We should not share the date of the event unless otherwise stated in the SOP, instead we should refer to a time period when the alleged behaviour occurred, e.g. ‘_in the month of July 2024’_;
* We should not share the allegation in detail, instead we should address the allegation by paraphrasing it in a professional manner, refraining from using slang or sharing excessive details. While it’s important to address the allegation, confidentiality must be maintained and specific information from the report cannot be shared, as that might endanger the reporting user, the police investigation and/or public safety.
* For safety incidents such as reports of rape, homicide, terrorism threat, abduction, illegal detainment, we should imply non-compliance with Terms and Conditions as the reason for suspending the accused user’s account for the duration of the internal investigation.
** _After 24h when the immediate threat has passed, we may share the allegation in a paraphrased manner._

!1f9ba@2x.png|width=44,height=44,alt=":safety_vest:"!

*Communicating the consequential action*

* When we consequently suspend a courier, we must notify them of the suspension/termination and the allegation via email too;
* When we suspend a fleet courier, we must notify the fleet owner via email simultaneously:
** This applies to both *investigative* and *consequential* suspensions. _This does not apply to when we consequently, after concluding the investigation, warn a courier;_
** We must also specify which fleet they are in association with and specify the date from which they are suspended/terminated.
* We must include references to T&C’s wording;
* Lastly, we must include a link where the courier can appeal our decision, if we have suspended their account or terminated the partnership with them.

I have reviewed 38 cases, of which 3 were detected by the supplier as having compliance issues:

# *Attachment Handling*: One issue involved an attachment that was not deleted. It contained a screenshot of a customer’s private chat, including their phone number, which led to a compliance issue due to sensitive information being mishandled.
# *Incorrect Compliance Scoring*: Two tickets were scored as compliance failures (unfortunately, comments were not added to the scoring). The chosen element was “User Verification,” which is not relevant in this scenario (both tickets are linked). In one of the tickets, there was an attachment, indicating that the supplier may have made a mistake and scored down the wrong element.
# *Missed Compliance on User Verification*: I reviewed 35 tickets that were scored 100% with no compliance issues detected. However, two of these tickets should have been scored down. In one, an inbound call was received from a non-registered profile. Although the agent found the correct driver, they did not verify the driver or request a call from the driver’s app. This means the verification process was not followed, and the user verification element should have been scored down.
# *Lost Item Process Error*: In another ticket, the agent mishandled the lost item process by sharing the rider’s phone number with the driver without receiving approval from the driver.

*Actions*

* *Attachment Handling*: Remind the supplier that screenshots and attachments should not be scored as “N/A.” Agents should also be reminded to delete any attachments containing sensitive information from Beehive.
* *Compliance Commenting*: Emphasize that it is essential to add comments explaining why compliance elements are scored down. Comments are crucial for agents to understand and improve their quality.
* *Lost Item Process Compliance*: Remind agents to follow the knowledge base (KB) guidelines on the lost item process. Phone numbers should not be shared without driver approval. Agents should first verify the item, identify the potential user, and only after confirmation, share the contact information.
* *Verification for Non-Registered Profiles*: Remind agents that when receiving calls from non-registered profiles, they should verify the user or request contact from the registered profile in the app.

{{When you enter a search term, we match your search with our index of partners (e.g. restaurant name) and product data (e.g. product description). These main parameters are applied with the help of certain algorithms, weightings and business internal rules. Accordingly, the text-based relevance influences with most weighting the position of the partner in the search results, after all search results have been previously grouped according to the opening hours. The popularity of the partner influences the results with the second importance in weighting and the partner's distance influences the results as the least important factor in weighting. The {{Faulty Equipment}} events which were removed from the Assessment Tool and that would require non-safety processes on how to handle are as follows:

* Faulty Brakes - An event in which the user reports faulty brakes or a non-accident event due to faulty brakes.
* Faulty Steering - An event in which the user reports faulty steering or a non-accident event due to fauly steering.
* Faulty Speedometer - An event in which the user reports faulty speedometer or a non-accident event due to faulty speedometer.
* Faulty Lights / Electronics - An event in which the user reports faulty lights/electronics or a non-accident event due to faulty lights/electronics.
* Faulty Wheels/Flat Tire - An event in which the user reports faulty wheels/flat tire or a non-accident event due to faulty wheels/flat tire.
* FaultySafety Equipment - An event in which the user reports that any of the safety equipment have failed (seatbelts, airbags etc)
* Mirrors or Windscreen Damaged - An event in which any of the mirrors or the windscreen is damaged.
* Document Issue - An event in which the cars registration or insurance or any other documents are not up to date.

Hey [~accountid:712020:2f68ebec-bff7-4acf-a855-0eeaf1c88737], thanks for reaching out!

*Overall, the project is completed (although not in a way we initially expected), and can be marked as done and closed. No further support is required from Commerce, Finance, Legal, Tax, etc.*

We have a Slack channel _#ua-business-setup-revamp-debt-collection_ where all details on the project are shared in real time.

Copying some of the high-level milestones:

* Initially, [we planned to move BB UA from 3P resale to a proper resale model|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C04BXFRAH52/p1677703970256359] either via resale through ‘Bolt Operations OÜ’, or via resale through Bolt’s local UA entity ‘Bolt Operations Ukraine LLC’.
* After working through countless issues with legal, licensing and banking limitations in UA, [getting external advice from Baker McKenzie|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C04BXFRAH52/p1689226793134719] and finally getting our potential working model [blocked by Citibank Ukraine|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C04BXFRAH52/p1710320939554119], it was deemed unfeasible to move from 3P resale to proper resale at least until the war in UA ends, or new legislation ‘on gig economy’ is passed.
* Due to having a [significant bad debt with the current 3P service provider (partner)|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C04BXFRAH52/p1717660892439029] it was decided to diversify and have a second 3P partner involved to reduce dependency on the initial partner and improve commercial side of the setup (new partner works with a smaller commission).
* The [contracts with the new 3P partner were signed |https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C04BXFRAH52/p1725529005163269?thread_ts=1724329856.043209&cid=C04BXFRAH52]in Sept. 2024 and the first actual clients were signed to the new partner in Oct. 2024. We’ll be testing the new payment setup in Nov. 2024 (when first clients receive their first invoices and new 3P partner makes his first payment to Bolt) and if everything works as expected, we’ll be transferring all BB UA clients from the old 3P partner to the new 3P partner.
* I expect the client transfer to be fully completed by the end of Q1 '25, but it will be done by BB UA team internally with no resources needed from Finance, Legal, Tax, etc.

Hope this helps and please make sure to tag me if new updates or anything else is required on this project.

Hi [~accountid:618bcc5c137a51006a5a95d6],

Regarding your question about the information and documentation required from fleets under the DSA regulation—specifically whether we need to request ID from fleet company directors when the fleets are structured as companies—the answer is no. Instead, you should request the following: i) the trade register in which the company is registered (if applicable) and ii) a copy of the registry extract or registration certificate of the company. The ID requirement is only applicable to individuals operating as sole traders.

Please see below for further details. You can also refer to the document: [Process on the traceability of traders|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1JF29fsN-tOSWuKk9WCyZX82p3LPeic78R9J434fdSQQ/edit?tab=t.0].

_“For the purposes of this policy, the traders are drivers and fleets._

# _Collect following information from the traders in EU as of 17th of Feb 2024:_
## _name, address, phone number, email address;_
## _payment account details;_
## _in case the trader is a legal entity (company):_
### _trade register in which the company is registered (if relevant);_
### _a copy of registry extract or registration certificate of the company;_
## _in case the trader is a natural person (i.e. providing service under his/her own name):_
### _a copy of the identification document of the person.”_



Additionally, in response to the GM's query about whether a Trade Register Excerpt can be replaced with a screenshot from the Ministry of Transport's website that includes the company name, registration number, address, and VTC licenses: Product Counsel believes that, for practicality, this can be substituted with a screenshot from the Spanish Transport Ministry’s website, provided it includes essential information (company name, registration number, address, VTC licenses) and is somehow time-stamped. I am aligned with this approach.

It’s important to highlight that the *sanctions for non-compliance can reach up to 6% of our annual global GMV.* I understand that a working group within the Ops team is focused on ensuring proper implementation. However, it is vital that we comply with the requirements without any delays.

If you have any questions or need further assistance, please feel free to reach out.

Thank you!

{noformat}const timestamp = moment()
    .utc()
    .subtract(0, "years")
    .subtract(6, "months")
    .subtract(0, "days")
    .unix();{noformat}

30 Oct 24  => 30 Apr 24
31 Oct 24  => 30 Apr 24  - April has 30 days 🤦‍♂️

Hey, 

Considering the examples raised here and my discussions with the PEX and CS Safety teams, we are planning to add a new Event to the [Assessment Tool|https://www.cognitoforms.com/Taxify1/globaleventassessmenttool2] to start further scoping the issue of {{Third Party Order Theft}} and collect data, next to {{Courier Commits Theft}}.

I’d like to understand if there are any processes that might overlap or that might have to be amended before we go ahead with it. Let me give an overview of the scenarios below:

h4. *Courier Commits Theft*

_An event in which the courier committed non-forceful theft, such as stealing without applying physical force or verbal threats._

# Courier (1) marks themselves “arrived at restaurant” and this can be validated from the order map. Courier (1) re-assigns the order, another courier (2) is assigned by the system and upon arriving at the restaurant, courier (2) realises the order has been already taken; or
# The provider confirms that a courier (1) showed a screenshot of the order, took the order, and then another courier (2) came to pick up the same order and the order was gone. The courier (2) reports the order as missing. We assume the courier (1) most likely shared a screenshot of the order with another person (2).

h4. Third Party Order Theft

_An event in which a third party committed non-forceful theft towards the provider by stealing the order, without applying physical force or verbal threats._

# Provider reports the order as stolen/already picked up, we first check for ‘Courier Commits Theft’. If we can not determine it was a Bolt courier from the information already provided:
## We ask for a security recording and ask the provider to describe the person who picked up the order.
## If we can not determine it was a Bolt courier or no recording was provided, then we should log it as {{Third Party Order Theft}}.

h4. Non-safety process of ‘Order Never Arrived’:

# Courier picks up the order successfully from the provider, but something happens during the trip, e.g. accident, damaged order, so the delivery is not completed, but the courier is proactive , responsive and lets us know that there is an issue with the delivery, solve as per regular non-safety process.
# If the courier disappears along the way, does not communicate with Bolt and does not provide information on what happened with/during the delivery over a reasonable time period, we should log it as {{Courier Commits Theft}}.
# Any other points to consider here? [~accountid:5f155fa05ee2c30023a32dc1] [~accountid:5f9197f8606d4000694ceed2] [~accountid:6125f1fc4f292300693d81d2] 
# [~accountid:5e21ae3209fe530ca9feee69], are there any overlapping non-safety Ticket Issues which might need to be changed, in addition to creating a new safety Ticket Issue for {{Third Party Order Theft}}?

Thanks and I appreciate the input!

Clause 10.9 does refers to Estonian law as the applicable law ,however, it is also stated that _“The statutory provisions on the limitation of the choice of law and on the applicability of mandatory provisions, in particular of the state in which the Client has his/her habitual residence as a consumer, shall remain unaffected (Article 6 (1) Rome I Regulation).“_  In practice, this means that, regardless of the chosen law in the contract, consumers retain the protections of the laws of their home country. Therefore, even if Estonian law is specified, Lithuanian consumers are still protected by the mandatory provisions of Lithuanian law. If Estonian law contradicts Lithuanian mandatory laws, the Lithuanian laws will apply and prevail. Thus, there is no need to change the applicable law from Estonian law.

Hi [~accountid:712020:eb9cd4dd-46ca-47c8-a985-9f940495724a],

To provide some background, the labour inspector in Cyprus is currently auditing fleet companies and individual couriers to ensure compliance with social security obligations. A few weeks ago, we received a request to provide specific information -such as names, company details, and earnings- for both fleet companies and independent couriers. In response, we submitted details for fleet companies (since this does not involve personal data) and requested the legal basis for disclosing personal data related to independent couriers. The labour inspector has now replied, citing what they consider to be the legal basis for requesting this personal data.

Regarding your second question, while I am not a Cypriot lawyer, a plain reading of Article 8(f) of the _Establishment of the Inspection Service at the Ministry of Labour, Welfare, and Social Insurance Law of 2020_ suggests that the labour inspector may indeed have a legal basis for the information request. The article specifies that inspectors have the authority to require documents and records essential for labor and social security compliance investigations, which includes obtaining information directly from individuals if relevant. This provision seems to support the inspector’s position:

_The Head of the Department, as well as any Inspector, for the purposes of implementing the provisions of this Law and the relevant law, has the authority to act as follows:_

*_(f)_* _To require any person whom they reasonably believe to be able to provide information related to any inspection, examination, interrogation, or investigation to respond to relevant questions, either alone or in the presence of any other person whose presence the Inspector may permit._



Many thanks!

Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

Hi ${user_firstname},

We aim to provide you with some important information:

You are considered independent data controllers under privacy regulations. This means that you are responsible for ensuring that your use of CCTV cameras aligns with local and EU laws, particularly with regard to privacy and data protection.

If you use CCTV cameras, we recommend that you ensure that you have the CCTV warning sign and enhance it by providing key details such as the purpose of the CCTV, the controller's name, the data retention period, and information on where customers can access a comprehensive CCTV privacy notice. We encourage you to review your Privacy Notices and ensure that it outlines how personal data from CCTV is processed. 

Kindly ensure that you inform customers about the processing of their personal data and CCTV records.

Please share your Privacy Notice with us so we can send it to the customers and inform them about how their data is being used by you in this case. 

Please be aware that non-compliance with these requirements could potentially lead to legal consequences due to breaches of privacy laws.

While we offer these recommendations, we want to emphasize that as independent data controllers, you have the autonomy to decide whether to follow our advice. However, it's important to note that you are accountable for any violations.

Hi Jana, thanks for reaching out.

The cancellation fee logic related to ETA was changed a while ago. Previously, cancellation fee logic added a cancellation fee if the *Current ETA/Original ETA < 80%*. With this logic, we would refund a cancellation fee if it was applied, but the ETA was exceeded.

However, we now have a new logic—the cancellation fee is not applied if *Elapsed Time + Remaining Time > Promised Time + Buffer*. You can read more about it [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02CUF8CFCZ/p1697013776090249]. 

All in all, with the new logic, if a cancellation fee was applied, even if the ETA was exceeded, we shouldn’t refund it as *it’s applied correctly*.

Let me know if you have further questions!

I will share here the thoughts of DLA regarding the issue with Curb:

* _According to the wording of the clause, the exclusivity obligation applies “during the entire period of this Agreement, but for no more than 25 months after the conclusion of the Agreement”. The interpretation of the clause that is most consistent with its wording is that the exclusivity obligation applies_ +_only_+ _during the period in which the agreement is in force. This means that: (i) the clause ceases to have effect once the contract has ended and (ii) it has a maximum duration of 25 months, so even if the contract lasts longer, the partner is only bound by this obligation for the first 25 months of the contract. In order to contradict the literal interpretation of the clause, Bolt would have to effectively demonstrate that the real will of the parties was different from the wording, namely that the parties wanted the obligation to be in force for the post-contractual period._
* _Therefore, in our opinion, it is unlikely that Bolt will be able to effectively apply the aforementioned sanctions against Curb._

Considering that (i) Curb’s interpretation of the exclusivity clause is not unreasonable (ii) the payment of the penalty would be dependent on the interpretation of the clause, and also (iii) that the next step will be to moving forward with a claim in Court, I think that from a cost-benefit perspective it is not favourable to go ahead with this.

Thank you

----

I looked what our competitors have:

Wolt (please be noted that Wolt had 24 or 48 hours earlier): Please note that in case of defects in foodstuffs or other products that by their nature spoil or age rapidly, it is crucial that you notify the defect *as soon as possible* to enable proper investigation and verification of the defect.

Foodora: We want you to be satisfied with our service! In the event of any missing items or if the Products you receive are faulty, incorrect or do not match your order, we kindly ask you to *immediately contact* our Help Center or customer service with pictures (if applicable) and description of the problem.

Just Eat: We have no control over Businesses and the quality of the Products or service that they provide, and Just Eat has no responsibility or liability for providing any compensation to you. If you are dissatisfied with the quality of any Products or the service provided by a Business and wish to seek a refund, a proportionate price reduction or any other compensation, *please let us know within 24 hours of placing your Order*.

----

That said, perishable goods must be in conformity with the contract at the time of delivery, meaning that if they are defective (e.g. spoiled upon arrival), consumers have the right to complain and request a refund. However, the time frame for complaints is often *limited to a reasonable period* based on the product's expected shelf life. Furthermore, EU Member States may set *specific time limits* for complaints on perishable goods. Some countries specify a few days or weeks as the allowable complaint period for food items or goods that spoil quickly. For example, consumers might be required to report issues within a few days of delivery for fresh food, dairy or other short-lived products, depending on national law.

----

*Based on the above, I suggest adding similar wording as Wolt and Foodora have: as soon as reasonably possible for foodstuff/perishable goods.* What do you think? We are going to update all T&Cs in Q1 (but it may take a bit longer as we are dependent on multiple local legal counsels). Please also be noted that we cannot apply the same for retail goods which foresee quite clear guidelines for complaints, +i.e. “as soon as reasonably possible” will only apply to foodstuff/perishable goods+.

Since Sweden’s reclass risk is not low, there are suggestions which should be followed when implementing Bolt Rewards, as follows:

# Ideally, Bolt Rewards would be offered to all drivers - this is the least risky approach and its effect on the reclass risk would be close to zero.
However, if that is not commercially viable then the scope of drivers that are able to participate in the program should be based on their +ride completion rate+ (e.g. complete 10 trips within a month and become part of Bolt Rewards program!). No other performance metrics of drivers should be considered when enabling them to use Bolt Rewards. Please also note that if completion rate is chosen, then the threshold of completed rides should not be a disproportionate and unrealistic number.
# Internal benefits are to be avoided. This includes the acceptance screen transparency feature (where only certain tier drivers can see the price and destination of the trip before acceptance). It is legal’s assessment that using such internal benefits would raise the reclass risk exponentially. Therefore, it should be avoided as to not raise Sweden’s risk level further.
# The third party offers as rewards should be low value offers such as mobile phone service vouchers, car washes, fuel cards, restaurant vouchers etc.
# When marketing and communicating with drivers about the program do not use terminology such as “loyalty program”, “loyalty level”, “loyalty points” etc.
